pt.title: [Logística 101 #5] Pare de tratar todos os itens da prateleira da mesma forma

segments.src: > Inventory isn't one problem — it's four questions: which items matter most, how little you can hold, who does the reordering, and how fast the whole pile moves.
segments.tr: > O estoque não é um problema só — são quatro perguntas: quais itens importam mais, quanto você pode manter em estoque no mínimo, quem faz a reposição e com que velocidade todo o conjunto gira.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: Every business that stocks anything faces the same tension.
segments.tr: Todo negócio que estoca qualquer coisa enfrenta a mesma tensão.

segments.src: Hold too much, and cash sits on a shelf getting dusty (and paying rent).
segments.tr: Estocar demais faz o dinheiro ficar parado numa prateleira acumulando poeira (e pagando aluguel).

segments.src: Hold too little, and you turn customers away.
segments.tr: Estocar de menos faz você perder clientes.

segments.src: The instinct is to solve this once, for everything.
segments.tr: A tendência é resolver isso de uma vez só, para tudo.

segments.src: That's the mistake.
segments.tr: Esse é o erro.

segments.src: A hardware store carries $80 cordless drills and 3-cent washers in the same building.
segments.tr: Uma loja de ferragens tem furadeiras sem fio de US$ 80 e arruelas de 3 centavos no mesmo prédio.

segments.src: Counting them with the same care is a waste of somebody's afternoon.
segments.tr: Contá-las com o mesmo cuidado é desperdiçar a tarde de alguém.

segments.src: Four tools handle this, and they stack:
segments.tr: Quatro ferramentas resolvem isso, e elas se complementam:

segments.src: ABC analysis — decide where to spend attention.**
segments.tr: Análise ABC — decida onde concentrar a atenção.**

segments.src: Rank every item by *annual dollar volume* (unit cost × units used per year), then split the list into three buckets.
segments.tr: Classifique todos os itens pelo *volume anual em dinheiro* (custo unitário × unidades usadas por ano) e depois divida a lista em três grupos.

segments.src: In a typical operation the pattern looks roughly like this:
segments.tr: Em uma operação típica, o padrão fica mais ou menos assim:

segments.src: - **A items:** ~20% of the items, ~80% of the dollars. Watch closely, count often, forecast carefully.
segments.tr: - **Itens A:** cerca de 20% dos itens, cerca de 80% do dinheiro. Acompanhe de perto, conte com frequência, faça previsões com cuidado.

segments.src: - **B items:** ~30% of the items, ~15% of the dollars. Moderate control.
segments.tr: - **Itens B:** cerca de 30% dos itens, cerca de 15% do dinheiro. Controle moderado.

segments.src: - **C items:** ~50% of the items, ~5% of the dollars. Order big, order rarely, don't agonize.
segments.tr: - **Itens C:** cerca de 50% dos itens, cerca de 5% do dinheiro. Peça em lotes grandes e com pouca frequência, e não se preocupe demais.

segments.src: Those percentages are a rule of thumb (the Pareto principle), not a law — your actual curve might be 15/85 or 30/70.
segments.tr: Esses percentuais são uma regra prática (o princípio de Pareto), não uma lei — sua curva real pode ser 15/85 ou 30/70.

segments.src: The point stands either way: attention is scarce, so aim it at the A items.
segments.tr: O ponto se mantém de qualquer forma: a atenção é escassa, então direcione-a para os itens A.

segments.src: One caveat that trips people up: dollar volume isn't the only thing that matters.
segments.tr: Uma ressalva que costuma confundir: o volume em dinheiro não é o único fator que importa.

segments.src: A 3-cent gasket that shuts down a production line is a C item by cost and an A item by consequence.
segments.tr: Uma junta de 3 centavos que para uma linha de produção é um item C pelo custo e um item A pelas consequências.

segments.src: Good practice is to override the ranking for anything that's critical, hard to source, or has a long lead time.
segments.tr: A boa prática é sobrepor a classificação para qualquer item crítico, difícil de obter ou com prazo de entrega longo.

segments.src: JIT (Just-In-Time) — shrink what you hold.**
segments.tr: JIT (Just-In-Time) — reduza o que você mantém em estoque.**

segments.src: Developed inside Toyota's production system, JIT means material arrives right when it's needed, in the quantity needed.
segments.tr: Desenvolvido dentro do sistema de produção da Toyota, o JIT significa que o material chega exatamente quando é necessário, na quantidade necessária.

segments.src: Instead of forecasting demand and pushing inventory forward, downstream consumption *pulls* the next delivery.
segments.tr: Em vez de prever a demanda e empurrar o estoque para frente, o consumo a jusante *puxa* a próxima entrega.

segments.src: The payoff is real: less cash tied up, less warehouse space, and defects surface fast because there's no buffer of bad parts to hide behind.
segments.tr: O ganho é real: menos capital imobilizado, menos espaço de armazenagem, e os defeitos aparecem rapidamente porque não há um colchão de peças ruins para escondê-los.

segments.src: The cost is equally real: JIT trades inventory buffer for supply-chain reliability.
segments.tr: O custo é igualmente real: o JIT troca o colchão de estoque por confiabilidade na cadeia de suprimentos.

segments.src: When something breaks upstream — a port backup, a chip shortage, a snowstorm on I-80 — you feel it in days, not months.
segments.tr: Quando algo quebra a montante — um congestionamento no porto, uma escassez de chips, uma nevasca na I-80 — você sente em dias, não em meses.

segments.src: That's why many firms after 2020 shifted toward "just-in-case" hybrids: JIT for stable, high-volume items; deliberate buffers for anything single-sourced or coming from far away.
segments.tr: Por isso, muitas empresas depois de 2020 migraram para híbridos do tipo “just-in-case”: JIT para itens estáveis e de alto volume; colchões deliberados para qualquer item com fonte única ou vindo de longe.

segments.src: VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory) — hand the reordering to the supplier.**
segments.tr: VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory) — passe a reposição para o fornecedor.**

segments.src: Normally the buyer decides when to reorder.
segments.tr: Normalmente, o comprador decide quando fazer o pedido de reposição.

segments.src: Under VMI, the buyer shares actual sales and stock data, and the *supplier* decides what to ship and when, within agreed min/max levels.
segments.tr: No VMI, o comprador compartilha os dados reais de vendas e de estoque, e o *fornecedor* decide o que enviar e quando, dentro de níveis mínimos e máximos acordados.

segments.src: Walmart and P&G built the best-known version of this in the late 1980s.
segments.tr: Walmart e P&G criaram a versão mais conhecida disso no final dos anos 1980.

segments.src: Why it helps: the supplier finally sees real demand instead of guessing from lumpy purchase orders.
segments.tr: Por que isso ajuda: o fornecedor finalmente enxerga a demanda real, em vez de adivinhar a partir de pedidos de compra irregulares.

segments.src: That damps the *bullwhip effect* — the way small wiggles in retail demand get amplified into wild swings in factory orders as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: Isso amortece o *efeito chicote* (bullwhip effect) — a forma como pequenas oscilações na demanda do varejo são amplificadas em grandes variações nos pedidos da fábrica à medida que sobem pela cadeia.

segments.src: Ownership of the goods may or may not transfer at delivery; that's a contract detail worth pinning down, because it decides who eats the cost of unsold stock.
segments.tr: A propriedade das mercadorias pode ou não ser transferida na entrega; esse é um detalhe contratual que vale a pena definir, porque determina quem arca com o custo do estoque não vendido.

segments.src: Inventory turnover — measure whether any of it is working.**
segments.tr: Giro de estoque — meça se algum deles está funcionando.**

segments.src: Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold ÷ Average Inventory
segments.tr: Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold ÷ Average Inventory

segments.src: Days of Inventory   = 365 ÷ Inventory Turnover
segments.tr: Days of Inventory   = 365 ÷ Inventory Turnover

segments.src: Turnover says how many times per year you sell through and replace your entire stock.
segments.tr: O giro indica quantas vezes por ano você vende e repõe todo o seu estoque.

segments.src: Use COGS, not revenue — revenue includes your margin, inventory is carried at cost, and mixing them inflates the number.
segments.tr: Use o CMV, não a receita — a receita inclui sua margem, enquanto o estoque é registrado pelo custo, e misturar os dois infla o número.

segments.src: Higher is generally better, but not infinitely.
segments.tr: Quanto maior, em geral melhor, mas não infinitamente.

segments.src: Turnover that's climbing while stockouts are also climbing means you've gone too lean.
segments.tr: Um giro crescente acompanhado de ruptura de estoque crescente significa que você ficou enxuto demais.

segments.src: And the "good" number is entirely industry-specific: a grocery chain may turn 12–15 times a year, a jeweler 1–2.
segments.tr: E o número “bom” depende totalmente do setor: uma rede de supermercados pode girar 12 a 15 vezes por ano, uma joalheria 1 a 2 vezes.

segments.src: Compare yourself to your own trend and your own sector, never to a headline benchmark from a different business.
segments.tr: Compare-se com a sua própria tendência e com o seu setor, nunca com um benchmark de manchete de um negócio diferente.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## No Dia a Dia

segments.src: Picture a three-location coffee shop in Austin.
segments.tr: Imagine uma cafeteria com três unidades em Austin.

segments.src: Annual COGS is $180,000, and average inventory on hand is $15,000.
segments.tr: O CMV anual é de US$ 180.000, e o estoque médio disponível é de US$ 15.000.

segments.src: Turnover = 180,000 ÷ 15,000 = 12 times per year
segments.tr: Turnover = 180,000 ÷ 15,000 = 12 times per year

segments.src: Days of inventory = 365 ÷ 12 ≈ 30 days
segments.tr: Days of inventory = 365 ÷ 12 ≈ 30 days

segments.src: Thirty days of stock — for a business selling milk and pastries.
segments.tr: Trinta dias de estoque — para um negócio que vende leite e doces.

segments.src: Something's off, and ABC analysis shows where.
segments.tr: Algo não está certo, e a análise ABC mostra onde.

segments.src: Espresso beans and oat milk are the **A items**: high cost, high volume, and they go stale.
segments.tr: Grãos de café espresso e leite de aveia são os **itens A**: custo alto, volume alto, e perdem o frescor.

segments.src: Flavored syrups are **B**.
segments.tr: Xaropes saborizados são **B**.

segments.src: Cups, lids, sleeves, and napkins are **C** — thousands of units, a few hundred dollars.
segments.tr: Copos, tampas, mangas térmicas e guardanapos são **C** — milhares de unidades, algumas centenas de dólares.

segments.src: So the owner splits the strategy.
segments.tr: Então o dono divide a estratégia.

segments.src: Beans move to near-JIT: twice-weekly roaster deliveries sized to last week's actual pours, plus a small safety buffer for the Saturday rush.
segments.tr: Os grãos passam para quase JIT: entregas do torrefador duas vezes por semana, dimensionadas para o consumo real da semana anterior, mais um pequeno colchão de segurança para o movimento de sábado.

segments.src: Pastries were already JIT — the bakery drops them at 5 a.m.
segments.tr: Os doces já funcionavam em JIT — a padaria entrega às 5 da manhã

segments.src: daily.
segments.tr: todos os dias.

segments.src: Cups go the other way: one big quarterly order, because the storage closet is cheaper than the hassle of reordering.
segments.tr: Os copos seguem o caminho oposto: um grande pedido trimestral, porque o armário de estoque custa menos do que a dor de cabeça de fazer pedidos com frequência.

segments.src: And that rack of chips and bottled drinks by the register?
segments.tr: E aquela prateleira de salgadinhos e bebidas engarrafadas perto do caixa?

segments.src: The distributor's driver already walks in, eyeballs the shelf, and restocks it without anyone at the shop writing a purchase order.
segments.tr: O motorista do distribuidor já passa por lá, olha a prateleira e a reabastece sem que ninguém na loja emita um pedido de compra.

segments.src: That's **VMI** — the same arrangement behind the vendor rep stocking the snack aisle at your local supermarket.
segments.tr: Isso é **VMI** — o mesmo arranjo por trás do representante do fornecedor que abastece o corredor de snacks do seu supermercado local.

segments.src: The shop stopped counting those items entirely.
segments.tr: A loja deixou de contar esses itens completamente.

segments.src: Six months later: average inventory is $10,000, turnover is 18, days of inventory is about 20.
segments.tr: Seis meses depois: o estoque médio é de US$ 10.000, o giro é 18, e os dias de estoque ficam em cerca de 20.

segments.src: Roughly $5,000 in cash walked off the shelf and back into the register — and the espresso never ran out.
segments.tr: Cerca de US$ 5.000 em caixa saíram da prateleira e voltaram para o caixa registrador — e o espresso nunca acabou.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumo em Três Linhas

segments.src: 1. **ABC analysis** ranks items by annual dollar volume so your attention goes to the 20% of items carrying 80% of the money — with manual overrides for anything mission-critical.
segments.tr: 1. **A análise ABC** classifica os itens pelo volume anual em dinheiro, para que sua atenção vá para os 20% dos itens que concentram 80% do dinheiro — com sobreposições manuais para qualquer item essencial à operação.

segments.src: 2. **JIT** replaces stock with reliable, frequent replenishment; **VMI** hands the reorder decision to a supplier who can finally see real demand.
segments.tr: 2. **JIT** substitui estoque por reposição confiável e frequente; **VMI** entrega a decisão de reposição a um fornecedor que finalmente consegue enxergar a demanda real.

segments.src: 3. **Inventory turnover (COGS ÷ average inventory)** is the scoreboard — read it alongside stockout rate, because "faster" is only better until customers start leaving empty-handed.
segments.tr: 3. **Giro de estoque (CMV ÷ estoque médio)** é o placar — leia-o junto com a taxa de ruptura, porque “mais rápido” só é melhor até os clientes começarem a sair de mãos vazias.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoavaliação

segments.src: **Q1.** A distributor stocks 1,000 SKUs.
segments.tr: **Q1.** Um distribuidor mantém 1.000 SKUs.

segments.src: Which items should get the tightest cycle counting and forecasting?
segments.tr: Quais itens devem receber a contagem cíclica e a previsão mais rigorosas?

segments.src: - (a) The 500 SKUs with the highest unit count
segments.tr: - (a) Os 500 SKUs com a maior quantidade de unidades

segments.src: - (b) The ~200 SKUs representing about 80% of annual dollar volume
segments.tr: - (b) Cerca de 200 SKUs que representam cerca de 80% do volume anual em dinheiro

segments.src: - (c) The cheapest SKUs, since errors there are easy to fix
segments.tr: - (c) Os SKUs mais baratos, já que erros ali são fáceis de corrigir

segments.src: - (d) Every SKU equally, for fairness
segments.tr: - (d) Todos os SKUs igualmente, por justiça

segments.src: **Q2.** A company reports COGS of $600,000 and average inventory of $50,000.
segments.tr: **Q2.** Uma empresa informa CMV de US$ 600.000 e estoque médio de US$ 50.000.

segments.src: What is inventory turnover, and roughly how many days of stock is that?
segments.tr: Qual é o giro de estoque e, aproximadamente, quantos dias de estoque isso representa?

segments.src: **Q3.** O/X — Under Vendor-Managed Inventory, the buyer keeps issuing the purchase orders and the supplier simply ships faster.
segments.tr: **Q3.** V/F — No Vendor-Managed Inventory, o comprador continua emitindo os pedidos de compra e o fornecedor simplesmente envia mais rápido.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **ABC Analysis** — Classifying inventory into A/B/C tiers by annual dollar volume so control effort matches financial impact.
segments.tr: - **Análise ABC** — Classificação do estoque em faixas A/B/C pelo volume anual em dinheiro, para que o esforço de controle acompanhe o impacto financeiro.

segments.src: - **JIT (Just-In-Time)** — A pull-based replenishment approach where material arrives only as it's needed, minimizing held stock at the cost of higher exposure to supply disruption.
segments.tr: - **JIT (Just-In-Time)** — Abordagem de reposição puxada pela demanda, em que o material chega apenas quando é necessário, minimizando o estoque mantido, ao custo de maior exposição a interrupções no fornecimento.

segments.src: - **VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)** — An arrangement where the supplier, using shared demand and stock data, decides replenishment timing and quantity within agreed limits.
segments.tr: - **VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)** — Arranjo em que o fornecedor, usando dados compartilhados de demanda e estoque, decide o momento e a quantidade da reposição dentro de limites acordados.

segments.src: - **Inventory Turnover** — COGS divided by average inventory; how many times a year stock is sold and replaced.
segments.tr: - **Giro de Estoque** — CMV dividido pelo estoque médio; quantas vezes por ano o estoque é vendido e reposto.

segments.src: - **Safety Stock** — Extra inventory held to absorb demand variability and supplier delay; the deliberate buffer that JIT tries to shrink but rarely eliminates.
segments.tr: - **Estoque de Segurança** — Estoque extra mantido para absorver a variabilidade da demanda e atrasos do fornecedor; o colchão deliberado que o JIT tenta reduzir, mas raramente elimina.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip Effect** — The amplification of demand swings as orders move upstream through a supply chain, driven by delayed and distorted information.
segments.tr: - **Efeito Chicote (Bullwhip Effect)** — A amplificação das oscilações da demanda à medida que os pedidos sobem pela cadeia de suprimentos, causada por informações atrasadas e distorcidas.

segments.src: *Answers:*
segments.tr: *Respostas:*

segments.tr: A ABC classifica pelo volume anual em dinheiro (custo unitário × uso anual), não apenas pela quantidade de unidades ou pelo preço unitário.

segments.src: The A tier is where tight control pays for itself.
segments.tr: A faixa A é onde o controle rigoroso se paga.

segments.src: Just remember the override: a cheap part that halts operations gets A-level treatment regardless of its dollar rank.*
segments.tr: Lembre-se apenas da sobreposição: uma peça barata que paralisa a operação recebe tratamento de nível A, independentemente da sua posição em dinheiro.*

segments.src: *Q2 — Turnover = 600,000 ÷ 50,000 = 12 times per year.
segments.tr: *Q2 — Giro = 600.000 ÷ 50.000 = 12 vezes por ano.

segments.tr: Dias de estoque = 365 ÷ 12 ≈ 30 dias.

segments.tr: Observe que o dado de entrada é CMV, não receita de vendas — usar a receita superestimaria o giro pelo valor da sua margem.*

segments.tr: *Q3 — F (Falso).

segments.tr: A característica definidora do VMI é que a decisão de reposição passa para o fornecedor, que trabalha com dados compartilhados de vendas e estoque dentro de níveis mínimos e máximos acordados.

segments.tr: - **Barang A:** ~20% dari jumlah barang, ~80% dari nilai dolar. Pantau dengan ketat, hitung sering, dan buat peramalan dengan cermat.

segments.src: - **B items:** ~30% of the items, ~15% of the dollars. Moderate control.
segments.tr: - **Barang B:** ~30% dari jumlah barang, ~15% dari nilai dolar. Pengendalian sedang.

segments.src: - **C items:** ~50% of the items, ~5% of the dollars. Order big, order rarely, don't agonize.
segments.tr: - **Barang C:** ~50% dari jumlah barang, ~5% dari nilai dolar. Pesan dalam jumlah besar, tetapi jarang, dan jangan terlalu dipusingkan.

segments.src: Those percentages are a rule of thumb (the Pareto principle), not a law — your actual curve might be 15/85 or 30/70.
segments.tr: Angka-angka tersebut hanyalah aturan praktis (prinsip Pareto), bukan hukum — kurva Anda mungkin 15/85 atau 30/70.

segments.src: The point stands either way: attention is scarce, so aim it at the A items.
segments.tr: Intinya tetap sama: perhatian itu terbatas, jadi arahkan ke barang A.

segments.src: One caveat that trips people up: dollar volume isn't the only thing that matters.
segments.tr: Satu catatan yang sering membuat orang keliru: nilai dolar bukan satu-satunya hal yang penting.

segments.src: A 3-cent gasket that shuts down a production line is a C item by cost and an A item by consequence.
segments.tr: Sebuah paking seharga 3 sen yang menghentikan lini produksi adalah barang C dilihat dari biaya dan barang A dilihat dari dampaknya.

segments.src: Good practice is to override the ranking for anything that's critical, hard to source, or has a long lead time.
segments.tr: Praktik yang baik adalah mengesampingkan peringkat untuk barang yang kritis, sulit didapat, atau memiliki waktu tunggu yang panjang.

segments.src: JIT (Just-In-Time) — shrink what you hold.**
segments.tr: JIT (Just-In-Time) — kurangi jumlah yang Anda simpan.**

segments.src: Developed inside Toyota's production system, JIT means material arrives right when it's needed, in the quantity needed.
segments.tr: Dikembangkan dalam sistem produksi Toyota, JIT berarti material tiba tepat saat dibutuhkan, dalam jumlah yang dibutuhkan.

segments.src: Instead of forecasting demand and pushing inventory forward, downstream consumption *pulls* the next delivery.
segments.tr: Alih-alih meramalkan permintaan lalu mendorong persediaan ke depan, konsumsi di hilir *menarik* pengiriman berikutnya.

segments.src: The payoff is real: less cash tied up, less warehouse space, and defects surface fast because there's no buffer of bad parts to hide behind.
segments.tr: Manfaatnya nyata: modal yang terikat lebih sedikit, ruang gudang lebih hemat, dan cacat cepat terlihat karena tidak ada penyangga suku cadang rusak untuk menutupinya.

segments.src: The cost is equally real: JIT trades inventory buffer for supply-chain reliability.
segments.tr: Biayanya juga nyata: JIT menukar penyangga persediaan dengan keandalan rantai pasok.

segments.src: When something breaks upstream — a port backup, a chip shortage, a snowstorm on I-80 — you feel it in days, not months.
segments.tr: Ketika sesuatu rusak di hulu — antrean di pelabuhan, kelangkaan chip, badai salju di I-80 — dampaknya terasa dalam hitungan hari, bukan bulan.

segments.src: That's why many firms after 2020 shifted toward "just-in-case" hybrids: JIT for stable, high-volume items; deliberate buffers for anything single-sourced or coming from far away.
segments.tr: Itulah sebabnya banyak perusahaan setelah 2020 beralih ke model hibrida "just-in-case": JIT untuk barang yang stabil dan bervolume tinggi; penyangga yang disengaja untuk barang yang bersumber dari satu pemasok atau berasal dari tempat yang jauh.

segments.src: VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory) — hand the reordering to the supplier.**
segments.tr: VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory) — serahkan pemesanan ulang kepada pemasok.**

segments.src: Normally the buyer decides when to reorder.
segments.tr: Biasanya pembeli yang memutuskan kapan memesan ulang.

segments.src: Under VMI, the buyer shares actual sales and stock data, and the *supplier* decides what to ship and when, within agreed min/max levels.
segments.tr: Dalam VMI, pembeli membagikan data penjualan dan stok yang sebenarnya, dan *pemasok* yang memutuskan apa yang dikirim dan kapan, dalam batas minimum/maksimum yang disepakati.

segments.src: Walmart and P&G built the best-known version of this in the late 1980s.
segments.tr: Walmart dan P&G membangun versi paling terkenal dari sistem ini pada akhir 1980-an.

segments.src: Why it helps: the supplier finally sees real demand instead of guessing from lumpy purchase orders.
segments.tr: Mengapa ini membantu: pemasok akhirnya melihat permintaan yang sebenarnya, alih-alih menebak dari pesanan pembelian yang tidak beraturan.

segments.src: That damps the *bullwhip effect* — the way small wiggles in retail demand get amplified into wild swings in factory orders as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: Hal ini meredam *efek cambuk (bullwhip effect)* — yaitu ketika fluktuasi kecil dalam permintaan ritel membesar menjadi ayunan liar pada pesanan pabrik saat bergerak ke hulu.

segments.src: Ownership of the goods may or may not transfer at delivery; that's a contract detail worth pinning down, because it decides who eats the cost of unsold stock.
segments.tr: Kepemilikan barang mungkin berpindah atau tidak saat pengiriman; ini adalah rincian kontrak yang perlu dipastikan, karena menentukan siapa yang menanggung biaya stok yang tidak terjual.

segments.src: Inventory turnover — measure whether any of it is working.**
segments.tr: Perputaran persediaan — ukur apakah semuanya bekerja dengan baik.**

segments.src: Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold ÷ Average Inventory
segments.tr: Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold ÷ Average Inventory

segments.src: Days of Inventory   = 365 ÷ Inventory Turnover
segments.tr: Days of Inventory   = 365 ÷ Inventory Turnover

segments.src: Turnover says how many times per year you sell through and replace your entire stock.
segments.tr: Perputaran menunjukkan berapa kali per tahun Anda menjual habis dan mengganti seluruh stok.

segments.src: Use COGS, not revenue — revenue includes your margin, inventory is carried at cost, and mixing them inflates the number.
segments.tr: Gunakan HPP (COGS), bukan pendapatan — pendapatan sudah mencakup margin Anda, sedangkan persediaan dicatat sebesar harga pokok, dan mencampur keduanya akan menggelembungkan angka.

segments.src: Higher is generally better, but not infinitely.
segments.tr: Angka yang lebih tinggi umumnya lebih baik, tetapi tidak tanpa batas.

segments.src: Turnover that's climbing while stockouts are also climbing means you've gone too lean.
segments.tr: Perputaran yang terus naik sementara kehabisan stok juga meningkat berarti Anda sudah terlalu ramping.

segments.src: And the "good" number is entirely industry-specific: a grocery chain may turn 12–15 times a year, a jeweler 1–2.
segments.tr: Dan angka "yang baik" sepenuhnya bergantung pada industri: rantai toko kelontong bisa berputar 12–15 kali setahun, sedangkan toko perhiasan 1–2 kali.

segments.src: Compare yourself to your own trend and your own sector, never to a headline benchmark from a different business.
segments.tr: Bandingkan diri Anda dengan tren Anda sendiri dan sektor Anda sendiri, jangan pernah dengan tolok ukur umum dari bisnis yang berbeda.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Picture a three-location coffee shop in Austin.
segments.tr: Bayangkan sebuah kedai kopi dengan tiga cabang di Austin.

segments.src: Annual COGS is $180,000, and average inventory on hand is $15,000.
segments.tr: HPP tahunannya $180.000, dan rata-rata persediaan yang ada adalah $15.000.

segments.src: Turnover = 180,000 ÷ 15,000 = 12 times per year
segments.tr: Turnover = 180,000 ÷ 15,000 = 12 times per year

segments.src: Days of inventory = 365 ÷ 12 ≈ 30 days
segments.tr: Days of inventory = 365 ÷ 12 ≈ 30 days

segments.src: Thirty days of stock — for a business selling milk and pastries.
segments.tr: Tiga puluh hari stok — untuk bisnis yang menjual susu dan kue.

segments.src: Something's off, and ABC analysis shows where.
segments.tr: Ada yang tidak beres, dan analisis ABC menunjukkan di mana letaknya.

segments.src: Espresso beans and oat milk are the **A items**: high cost, high volume, and they go stale.
segments.tr: Biji espresso dan susu oat adalah **barang A**: biaya tinggi, volume tinggi, dan cepat basi.

segments.src: Flavored syrups are **B**.
segments.tr: Sirup rasa termasuk **B**.

segments.src: Cups, lids, sleeves, and napkins are **C** — thousands of units, a few hundred dollars.
segments.tr: Gelas, tutup, sleeve, dan tisu termasuk **C** — ribuan unit, hanya beberapa ratus dolar.

segments.src: So the owner splits the strategy.
segments.tr: Jadi pemilik membagi strateginya.

segments.src: Beans move to near-JIT: twice-weekly roaster deliveries sized to last week's actual pours, plus a small safety buffer for the Saturday rush.
segments.tr: Biji kopi diatur mendekati JIT: pengiriman dari penyangrai dua kali seminggu, disesuaikan dengan jumlah seduhan minggu lalu, ditambah penyangga kecil untuk keramaian Sabtu.

segments.src: Pastries were already JIT — the bakery drops them at 5 a.m.
segments.tr: Kue sudah menerapkan JIT — toko roti mengantarkannya setiap hari pukul 5 pagi.

segments.src: daily.
segments.tr: setiap hari.

segments.src: Cups go the other way: one big quarterly order, because the storage closet is cheaper than the hassle of reordering.
segments.tr: Gelas justru sebaliknya: satu pesanan besar setiap kuartal, karena ruang penyimpanan lebih murah daripada repotnya memesan ulang.

segments.src: And that rack of chips and bottled drinks by the register?
segments.tr: Dan rak keripik serta minuman botol di dekat kasir?

segments.src: The distributor's driver already walks in, eyeballs the shelf, and restocks it without anyone at the shop writing a purchase order.
segments.tr: Sopir distributor sudah datang sendiri, memeriksa rak, dan mengisinya kembali tanpa seorang pun di toko membuat surat pesanan pembelian.

segments.src: That's **VMI** — the same arrangement behind the vendor rep stocking the snack aisle at your local supermarket.
segments.tr: Itulah **VMI** — pengaturan yang sama di balik perwakilan vendor yang mengisi lorong camilan di supermarket dekat rumah Anda.

segments.src: The shop stopped counting those items entirely.
segments.tr: Toko itu berhenti menghitung barang-barang tersebut sepenuhnya.

segments.src: Six months later: average inventory is $10,000, turnover is 18, days of inventory is about 20.
segments.tr: Enam bulan kemudian: rata-rata persediaan $10.000, perputaran 18, dan hari persediaan sekitar 20.

segments.src: Roughly $5,000 in cash walked off the shelf and back into the register — and the espresso never ran out.
segments.tr: Sekitar $5.000 uang tunai keluar dari rak dan kembali ke kasir — dan espresso tidak pernah habis.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. **ABC analysis** ranks items by annual dollar volume so your attention goes to the 20% of items carrying 80% of the money — with manual overrides for anything mission-critical.
segments.tr: 1. **Analisis ABC** mengurutkan barang berdasarkan nilai dolar tahunan agar perhatian Anda tertuju pada 20% barang yang menyumbang 80% uang — dengan pengesampingan manual untuk barang yang sangat penting.

segments.src: 2. **JIT** replaces stock with reliable, frequent replenishment; **VMI** hands the reorder decision to a supplier who can finally see real demand.
segments.tr: 2. **JIT** menggantikan stok dengan pengisian ulang yang andal dan sering; **VMI** menyerahkan keputusan pemesanan ulang kepada pemasok yang akhirnya dapat melihat permintaan yang sebenarnya.

segments.src: 3. **Inventory turnover (COGS ÷ average inventory)** is the scoreboard — read it alongside stockout rate, because "faster" is only better until customers start leaving empty-handed.
segments.tr: 3. **Perputaran persediaan (HPP ÷ rata-rata persediaan)** adalah papan skornya — baca bersama tingkat kehabisan stok, karena "lebih cepat" hanya lebih baik sampai pelanggan mulai pergi dengan tangan kosong.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **Q1.** A distributor stocks 1,000 SKUs.
segments.tr: **Q1.** Sebuah distributor menyimpan 1.000 SKU.

segments.src: Which items should get the tightest cycle counting and forecasting?
segments.tr: Barang mana yang harus mendapat penghitungan siklus dan peramalan paling ketat?

segments.src: - (a) The 500 SKUs with the highest unit count
segments.tr: - (a) 500 SKU dengan jumlah unit tertinggi

segments.src: - (b) The ~200 SKUs representing about 80% of annual dollar volume
segments.tr: - (b) Sekitar 200 SKU yang mewakili sekitar 80% dari nilai dolar tahunan

segments.src: - (c) The cheapest SKUs, since errors there are easy to fix
segments.tr: - (c) SKU termurah, karena kesalahan di sana mudah diperbaiki

segments.src: - (d) Every SKU equally, for fairness
segments.tr: - (d) Setiap SKU sama rata, demi keadilan

segments.src: **Q2.** A company reports COGS of $600,000 and average inventory of $50,000.
segments.tr: **Q2.** Sebuah perusahaan melaporkan HPP $600.000 dan rata-rata persediaan $50.000.

segments.src: What is inventory turnover, and roughly how many days of stock is that?
segments.tr: Berapa perputaran persediaannya, dan kira-kira berapa hari stok itu?

segments.src: **Q3.** O/X — Under Vendor-Managed Inventory, the buyer keeps issuing the purchase orders and the supplier simply ships faster.
segments.tr: **Q3.** B/S — Di bawah Vendor-Managed Inventory, pembeli tetap menerbitkan pesanan pembelian dan pemasok hanya mengirim lebih cepat.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **ABC Analysis** — Classifying inventory into A/B/C tiers by annual dollar volume so control effort matches financial impact.
segments.tr: - **Analisis ABC** — Mengelompokkan persediaan ke dalam tingkat A/B/C berdasarkan nilai dolar tahunan agar upaya pengendalian sesuai dengan dampak finansialnya.

segments.src: - **JIT (Just-In-Time)** — A pull-based replenishment approach where material arrives only as it's needed, minimizing held stock at the cost of higher exposure to supply disruption.
segments.tr: - **JIT (Just-In-Time)** — Pendekatan pengisian ulang berbasis tarikan (pull) di mana material tiba hanya saat dibutuhkan, meminimalkan stok yang ditahan dengan risiko lebih besar terhadap gangguan pasokan.

segments.src: - **VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)** — An arrangement where the supplier, using shared demand and stock data, decides replenishment timing and quantity within agreed limits.
segments.tr: - **VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)** — Pengaturan di mana pemasok, menggunakan data permintaan dan stok bersama, memutuskan waktu dan jumlah pengisian ulang dalam batas yang disepakati.

segments.src: - **Inventory Turnover** — COGS divided by average inventory; how many times a year stock is sold and replaced.
segments.tr: - **Perputaran Persediaan** — HPP dibagi rata-rata persediaan; berapa kali dalam setahun stok terjual dan diganti.

segments.src: - **Safety Stock** — Extra inventory held to absorb demand variability and supplier delay; the deliberate buffer that JIT tries to shrink but rarely eliminates.
segments.tr: - **Stok Pengaman** — Persediaan tambahan yang disimpan untuk menyerap variasi permintaan dan keterlambatan pemasok; penyangga yang sengaja disediakan, yang coba dikurangi oleh JIT tetapi jarang benar-benar dihilangkan.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip Effect** — The amplification of demand swings as orders move upstream through a supply chain, driven by delayed and distorted information.
segments.tr: - **Efek Cambuk (Bullwhip Effect)** — Pembesaran fluktuasi permintaan saat pesanan bergerak ke hulu rantai pasok, didorong oleh informasi yang tertunda dan terdistorsi.

segments.src: *Answers:*
segments.tr: *Jawaban:*

segments.src: ABC ranks by annual dollar volume (unit cost × annual usage), not unit count or unit price alone.
segments.tr: ABC mengurutkan berdasarkan nilai dolar tahunan (harga satuan × penggunaan tahunan), bukan jumlah unit atau harga satuan saja.

segments.src: The A tier is where tight control pays for itself.
segments.tr: Tingkat A adalah tempat pengendalian ketat terbayar dengan sendirinya.

segments.src: Just remember the override: a cheap part that halts operations gets A-level treatment regardless of its dollar rank.*
segments.tr: Ingat pengecualiannya: suku cadang murah yang menghentikan operasi mendapat perlakuan tingkat A terlepas dari peringkat nilai dolarnya.*

segments.src: *Q2 — Turnover = 600,000 ÷ 50,000 = 12 times per year.
segments.tr: *Q2 — Perputaran = 600.000 ÷ 50.000 = 12 kali per tahun.

segments.src: Days of inventory = 365 ÷ 12 ≈ 30 days.
segments.tr: Hari persediaan = 365 ÷ 12 ≈ 30 hari.

segments.src: Note the input is COGS, not sales revenue — using revenue would overstate turnover by the amount of your margin.*
segments.tr: Perhatikan bahwa masukannya adalah HPP, bukan pendapatan penjualan — menggunakan pendapatan akan melebih-lebihkan perputaran sebesar margin Anda.*

segments.src: *Q3 — X (False).
segments.tr: *Q3 — S (Salah).

segments.src: The defining feature of VMI is that the reorder decision moves to the supplier, who works from shared sales and inventory data within agreed min/max levels.
segments.tr: Ciri utama VMI adalah keputusan pemesanan ulang berpindah ke pemasok, yang bekerja berdasarkan data penjualan dan persediaan bersama dalam batas minimum/maksimum yang disepakati.

segments.src: If the buyer is still writing the POs, it's just a responsive vendor, not VMI.*
segments.tr: Jika pembeli masih menerbitkan PO, itu hanyalah vendor yang responsif, bukan VMI.*

ja.title: [Logistics 101 #5] 棚のすべての商品を同じように扱うのはやめよう

segments.src: > Inventory isn't one problem — it's four questions: which items matter most, how little you can hold, who does the reordering, and how fast the whole pile moves.
segments.tr: > 在庫は一つの問題ではなく、四つの問いです。どの商品が最も重要か、どれだけ少なく持てるか、補充は誰が行うか、そして在庫全体がどれだけ速く動くか、ということです。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Every business that stocks anything faces the same tension.
segments.tr: 在庫を扱うあらゆる事業は、同じ緊張関係に直面します。

segments.src: Hold too much, and cash sits on a shelf getting dusty (and paying rent).
segments.tr: 在庫を持ちすぎれば、現金は棚で埃をかぶり（そして家賃を払い続けることになります）。

segments.src: Hold too little, and you turn customers away.
segments.tr: 在庫が少なすぎれば、顧客を逃がすことになります。

segments.src: The instinct is to solve this once, for everything.
segments.tr: つい、すべてを一度に一括で解決しようとしがちです。

segments.src: That's the mistake.
segments.tr: それが間違いです。

segments.src: A hardware store carries $80 cordless drills and 3-cent washers in the same building.
segments.tr: ある金物店には、80ドルのコードレスドリルと3セントのワッシャーが同じ建物に置かれています。

segments.src: Counting them with the same care is a waste of somebody's afternoon.
segments.tr: それらを同じ手間をかけて数えるのは、誰かの午後を無駄にするだけです。

segments.src: Four tools handle this, and they stack:
segments.tr: この問題には四つのツールが役立ち、それらは組み合わせて使えます。

segments.src: ABC analysis — decide where to spend attention.**
segments.tr: ABC分析 ― 注意をどこに払うかを決める。**

segments.src: Rank every item by *annual dollar volume* (unit cost × units used per year), then split the list into three buckets.
segments.tr: すべての商品を*年間金額*（単価 × 年間使用量）で順位付けし、その一覧を三つのグループに分けます。

segments.src: In a typical operation the pattern looks roughly like this:
segments.tr: 一般的な運用では、おおよそ次のようなパターンになります。

segments.src: - **A items:** ~20% of the items, ~80% of the dollars. Watch closely, count often, forecast carefully.
segments.tr: - **A品目:** 全品目の約20%、金額の約80%。注意深く監視し、頻繁に数え、慎重に需要予測を行います。

segments.src: - **B items:** ~30% of the items, ~15% of the dollars. Moderate control.
segments.tr: - **B品目:** 全品目の約30%、金額の約15%。中程度の管理を行います。

segments.src: - **C items:** ~50% of the items, ~5% of the dollars. Order big, order rarely, don't agonize.
segments.tr: - **C品目:** 全品目の約50%、金額の約5%。まとめて大量に、めったに発注せず、細かく悩みすぎないようにします。

segments.src: Those percentages are a rule of thumb (the Pareto principle), not a law — your actual curve might be 15/85 or 30/70.
segments.tr: これらの割合は経験則（パレートの法則）であり、法則ではありません。実際の分布は15/85や30/70かもしれません。

segments.src: The point stands either way: attention is scarce, so aim it at the A items.
segments.tr: いずれにせよ要点は変わりません。注意力は限られているので、A品目に向けるべきです。

segments.src: One caveat that trips people up: dollar volume isn't the only thing that matters.
segments.tr: よくつまずく注意点があります。金額だけが重要なわけではありません。

segments.src: A 3-cent gasket that shuts down a production line is a C item by cost and an A item by consequence.
segments.tr: 3セントのガスケットが生産ラインを止めてしまうなら、コストで見ればC品目ですが、影響で見ればA品目です。

segments.src: Good practice is to override the ranking for anything that's critical, hard to source, or has a long lead time.
segments.tr: 良い実践としては、重大な品目、調達が困難な品目、リードタイムが長い品目について、順位付けを上書きすることです。

segments.src: JIT (Just-In-Time) — shrink what you hold.**
segments.tr: JIT（ジャスト・イン・タイム） ― 持つ在庫を減らす。**

segments.src: Developed inside Toyota's production system, JIT means material arrives right when it's needed, in the quantity needed.
segments.tr: トヨタの生産方式の中で生まれたJITとは、必要なときに、必要な量だけ部材が届くことを意味します。

segments.src: Instead of forecasting demand and pushing inventory forward, downstream consumption *pulls* the next delivery.
segments.tr: 需要を予測して在庫を前に押し出すのではなく、下流での消費が次の納品を*引き出す*のです。

segments.src: The payoff is real: less cash tied up, less warehouse space, and defects surface fast because there's no buffer of bad parts to hide behind.
segments.tr: そのメリットは現実的です。現金の拘束が減り、倉庫スペースも減り、不良品を隠すバッファがないため欠陥がすぐに表面化します。

segments.src: The cost is equally real: JIT trades inventory buffer for supply-chain reliability.
segments.tr: コストも同じくらい現実的です。JITは在庫のバッファと引き換えに、サプライチェーンの信頼性を手放すのです。

segments.src: When something breaks upstream — a port backup, a chip shortage, a snowstorm on I-80 — you feel it in days, not months.
segments.tr: 上流で何かが途絶えると ― 港の混雑、半導体不足、I-80での大雪など ― 数か月ではなく数日で影響を感じます。

segments.src: That's why many firms after 2020 shifted toward "just-in-case" hybrids: JIT for stable, high-volume items; deliberate buffers for anything single-sourced or coming from far away.
segments.tr: そのため2020年以降、多くの企業は「ジャスト・イン・ケース」型のハイブリッドへ移行しました。安定した大量の品目にはJIT、単一供給源や遠方から調達する品目には意図的なバッファを持たせる、というやり方です。

segments.src: VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory) — hand the reordering to the supplier.**
segments.tr: VMI（ベンダー管理在庫） ― 補充の判断をサプライヤーに任せる。**

segments.src: Normally the buyer decides when to reorder.
segments.tr: 通常、補充のタイミングを決めるのは購入側です。

segments.src: Under VMI, the buyer shares actual sales and stock data, and the *supplier* decides what to ship and when, within agreed min/max levels.
segments.tr: VMIでは、購入側が実際の販売データと在庫データを共有し、合意された最小・最大在庫の範囲内で、*サプライヤー*が何をいつ出荷するかを決めます。

segments.src: Walmart and P&G built the best-known version of this in the late 1980s.
segments.tr: ウォルマートとP&Gは1980年代後半に、この方式の最も有名な例を作り上げました。

segments.src: Why it helps: the supplier finally sees real demand instead of guessing from lumpy purchase orders.
segments.tr: それが役立つ理由は、サプライヤーが不規則な発注書から推測するのではなく、実際の需要を直接把握できるからです。

segments.src: That damps the *bullwhip effect* — the way small wiggles in retail demand get amplified into wild swings in factory orders as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: これによって*ブルウィップ効果*が抑えられます。これは、小売の需要のわずかな揺らぎが、上流へ伝わるにつれて工場への発注量の大きな振れに増幅される現象です。

segments.src: Ownership of the goods may or may not transfer at delivery; that's a contract detail worth pinning down, because it decides who eats the cost of unsold stock.
segments.tr: 商品の所有権が納品時に移転するかどうかは契約次第であり、契約上確認しておくべき点です。売れ残った在庫のコストを誰が負担するかを決めるからです。

segments.src: Inventory turnover — measure whether any of it is working.**
segments.tr: 在庫回転率 ― そのどれかが機能しているかを測る。**

segments.src: Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold ÷ Average Inventory
segments.tr: Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold ÷ Average Inventory

segments.src: Days of Inventory   = 365 ÷ Inventory Turnover
segments.tr: Days of Inventory   = 365 ÷ Inventory Turnover

segments.src: Turnover says how many times per year you sell through and replace your entire stock.
segments.tr: 在庫回転率とは、年間で在庫全体を何回売り切り、補充するかを示す数値です。

segments.src: Use COGS, not revenue — revenue includes your margin, inventory is carried at cost, and mixing them inflates the number.
segments.tr: 売上高ではなく売上原価（COGS）を使ってください。売上高には利益が含まれ、在庫は原価で計上されるため、両者を混ぜると数値が膨らみます。

segments.src: Higher is generally better, but not infinitely.
segments.tr: 高いほど一般的には良いですが、無限に良いわけではありません。

segments.src: Turnover that's climbing while stockouts are also climbing means you've gone too lean.
segments.tr: 在庫切れも増えているのに回転率が上がっているなら、在庫を絞りすぎています。

segments.src: And the "good" number is entirely industry-specific: a grocery chain may turn 12–15 times a year, a jeweler 1–2.
segments.tr: そして「良い」数値は業界によってまったく異なります。食料品チェーンは年間12〜15回転、宝飾店は1〜2回転かもしれません。

segments.src: Compare yourself to your own trend and your own sector, never to a headline benchmark from a different business.
segments.tr: 自社の推移と自社の業界とだけ比較し、別業種の見出しになるようなベンチマークとは比べないでください。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活の中で

segments.src: Picture a three-location coffee shop in Austin.
segments.tr: オースティンにある三店舗のコーヒーショップを想像してください。

segments.src: Annual COGS is $180,000, and average inventory on hand is $15,000.
segments.tr: 年間売上原価は18万ドルで、平均在庫は手元に1万5千ドルあります。

segments.src: Turnover = 180,000 ÷ 15,000 = 12 times per year
segments.tr: Turnover = 180,000 ÷ 15,000 = 12 times per year

segments.src: Days of inventory = 365 ÷ 12 ≈ 30 days
segments.tr: Days of inventory = 365 ÷ 12 ≈ 30 days

segments.src: Thirty days of stock — for a business selling milk and pastries.
segments.tr: これは牛乳とペストリーを扱う店にとって30日分の在庫です。

segments.src: Something's off, and ABC analysis shows where.
segments.tr: 何かがおかしく、ABC分析がその場所を示します。

segments.src: Espresso beans and oat milk are the **A items**: high cost, high volume, and they go stale.
segments.tr: エスプレッソ豆とオーツミルクは**A品目**です。原価が高く、量も多く、しかも劣化しやすい。

segments.src: Flavored syrups are **B**.
segments.tr: フレーバーシロップは**B**です。

segments.src: Cups, lids, sleeves, and napkins are **C** — thousands of units, a few hundred dollars.
segments.tr: カップ、蓋、スリーブ、ナプキンは**C**です。数千個単位でも、合計はわずか数百ドルです。

segments.src: So the owner splits the strategy.
segments.tr: そこでオーナーは戦略を分けました。

segments.src: Beans move to near-JIT: twice-weekly roaster deliveries sized to last week's actual pours, plus a small safety buffer for the Saturday rush.
segments.tr: 豆は限りなくJITに近い運用にします。先週の実際の抽出量に合わせて、週2回のロースターからの納品とし、土曜の混雑に備えた小さな安全バッファを加えます。

segments.src: Pastries were already JIT — the bakery drops them at 5 a.m.
segments.tr: ペストリーはもともとJITでした。パン屋が午前5時に

segments.src: daily.
segments.tr: 毎日届けてくれます。

segments.src: Cups go the other way: one big quarterly order, because the storage closet is cheaper than the hassle of reordering.
segments.tr: カップは逆です。四半期に一度の大口発注にします。保管室のスペースの方が、頻繁な再発注の手間よりも安くつくからです。

segments.src: And that rack of chips and bottled drinks by the register?
segments.tr: そして、レジ横にあるチップスとペットボトル飲料の棚はどうでしょう。

segments.src: The distributor's driver already walks in, eyeballs the shelf, and restocks it without anyone at the shop writing a purchase order.
segments.tr: 販売店の配送ドライバーがすでに店に入り、棚を目で確認して、店の誰も発注書を書かずに補充していきます。

segments.src: That's **VMI** — the same arrangement behind the vendor rep stocking the snack aisle at your local supermarket.
segments.tr: これが**VMI**です。近所のスーパーのスナック売り場を、ベンダーの担当者が補充しているのと同じ仕組みです。

segments.src: The shop stopped counting those items entirely.
segments.tr: 店はそれらの品目を数えることを完全にやめました。

segments.src: Six months later: average inventory is $10,000, turnover is 18, days of inventory is about 20.
segments.tr: 半年後：平均在庫は1万ドル、回転率は18、在庫日数は約20日になりました。

segments.src: Roughly $5,000 in cash walked off the shelf and back into the register — and the espresso never ran out.
segments.tr: 約5千ドルの現金が、棚からレジへと戻ってきたのです。そして、エスプレッソが切れることは一度もありませんでした。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行まとめ

segments.src: 1. **ABC analysis** ranks items by annual dollar volume so your attention goes to the 20% of items carrying 80% of the money — with manual overrides for anything mission-critical.
segments.tr: 1. **ABC分析**は、年間金額で商品を順位付けし、お金の80%を占める20%の商品に注意を集中させます。ただし、ミッションクリティカルな品目は手動で上書きします。

segments.src: 2. **JIT** replaces stock with reliable, frequent replenishment; **VMI** hands the reorder decision to a supplier who can finally see real demand.
segments.tr: 2. **JIT**は、在庫の代わりに、確実で頻繁な補充に置き換えます。**VMI**は、実際の需要を把握できるサプライヤーに発注の判断を任せます。

segments.src: 3. **Inventory turnover (COGS ÷ average inventory)** is the scoreboard — read it alongside stockout rate, because "faster" is only better until customers start leaving empty-handed.
segments.tr: 3. **在庫回転率（売上原価 ÷ 平均在庫）**は成績表です。在庫切れ率と合わせて読みましょう。「速い」ことは、顧客が手ぶらで帰り始めるまでしか良いことではないからです。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自己診断クイズ

segments.src: **Q1.** A distributor stocks 1,000 SKUs.
segments.tr: **Q1.** ある卸売業者が1,000のSKUを在庫しています。

segments.src: Which items should get the tightest cycle counting and forecasting?
segments.tr: 最も厳密な周期棚卸しと需要予測を行うべきなのは、どの商品でしょうか？

segments.src: - (a) The 500 SKUs with the highest unit count
segments.tr: - (a) 数量が最も多い500のSKU

segments.src: - (b) The ~200 SKUs representing about 80% of annual dollar volume
segments.tr: - (b) 年間金額の約80%を占める約200のSKU

segments.src: - (c) The cheapest SKUs, since errors there are easy to fix
segments.tr: - (c) 最も安いSKU。そこでのミスは修正しやすいから

segments.src: - (d) Every SKU equally, for fairness
segments.tr: - (d) 公平を期して、すべてのSKUを同じように

segments.src: **Q2.** A company reports COGS of $600,000 and average inventory of $50,000.
segments.tr: **Q2.** ある企業の売上原価は60万ドル、平均在庫は5万ドルと報告されています。

segments.src: What is inventory turnover, and roughly how many days of stock is that?
segments.tr: 在庫回転率はいくつで、それは在庫日数にするとおよそ何日分でしょうか？

segments.src: **Q3.** O/X — Under Vendor-Managed Inventory, the buyer keeps issuing the purchase orders and the supplier simply ships faster.
segments.tr: **Q3.** ○/×：ベンダー管理在庫（VMI）では、購入側が引き続き発注書を発行し、サプライヤーはただ速く出荷するだけである。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日の用語

segments.src: - **ABC Analysis** — Classifying inventory into A/B/C tiers by annual dollar volume so control effort matches financial impact.
segments.tr: - **ABC分析** — 年間金額によって在庫をA/B/Cの区分に分類し、管理の労力を財務的影響に見合ったものにすること。

segments.src: - **JIT (Just-In-Time)** — A pull-based replenishment approach where material arrives only as it's needed, minimizing held stock at the cost of higher exposure to supply disruption.
segments.tr: - **JIT（ジャスト・イン・タイム）** — 必要なときにだけ材料が届くプル型の補充方式。保有在庫を最小化する一方、供給途絶へのリスクが高まる。

segments.src: - **VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)** — An arrangement where the supplier, using shared demand and stock data, decides replenishment timing and quantity within agreed limits.
segments.tr: - **VMI（ベンダー管理在庫）** — サプライヤーが共有された需要と在庫のデータを使い、合意された範囲内で補充のタイミングと数量を決める仕組み。

segments.src: - **Inventory Turnover** — COGS divided by average inventory; how many times a year stock is sold and replaced.
segments.tr: - **在庫回転率** — 売上原価を平均在庫で割ったもの。年間に在庫が売れて補充される回数。

segments.src: - **Safety Stock** — Extra inventory held to absorb demand variability and supplier delay; the deliberate buffer that JIT tries to shrink but rarely eliminates.
segments.tr: - **安全在庫** — 需要の変動やサプライヤーの遅延を吸収するために保有する追加の在庫。JITが縮小しようとするが、ほとんど無くすことはできない、意図的なバッファ。

segments.src: - **Bullwhip Effect** — The amplification of demand swings as orders move upstream through a supply chain, driven by delayed and distorted information.
segments.tr: - **ブルウィップ効果** — 遅延と歪んだ情報によって、サプライチェーンを上流へ遡るにつれて需要の振れが増幅される現象。

segments.src: *Answers:*
segments.tr: *解答：*

segments.src: ABC ranks by annual dollar volume (unit cost × annual usage), not unit count or unit price alone.
segments.tr: ABCは年間金額（単価 × 年間使用量）で順位付けします。数量や単価だけで順位付けするわけではありません。

segments.src: The A tier is where tight control pays for itself.
segments.tr: A区分は、厳格な管理が費用対効果を発揮する領域です。

segments.src: Just remember the override: a cheap part that halts operations gets A-level treatment regardless of its dollar rank.*
segments.tr: ただし上書きのルールを忘れないでください。業務を止めてしまう安価な部品は、金額順位にかかわらずA級の扱いを受けます。*

segments.src: *Q2 — Turnover = 600,000 ÷ 50,000 = 12 times per year.
Days of inventory = 365 ÷ 12 ≈ 30 days.
Note the input is COGS, not sales revenue — using revenue would overstate turnover by the amount of your margin.*
segments.tr: 入力は売上高ではなく売上原価であることに注意してください。売上高を使うと、回転率は利益率の分だけ過大に出ます。*

segments.src: *Q3 — X (False).
The defining feature of VMI is that the reorder decision moves to the supplier, who works from shared sales and inventory data within agreed min/max levels.
segments.tr: VMIの決定的な特徴は、発注の判断がサプライヤーに移ることです。サプライヤーは、合意された最小・最大在庫の範囲内で、共有された販売データと在庫データをもとに動きます。

segments.src: If the buyer is still writing the POs, it's just a responsive vendor, not VMI.*
segments.tr: 購入側がまだ発注書を書いているなら、それは反応の速いベンダーにすぎず、VMIではありません。*

de.title: [Logistik 101 #5] Nicht jeden Artikel im Regal gleich behandeln

segments.src: > Inventory isn't one problem — it's four questions: which items matter most, how little you can hold, who does the reordering, and how fast the whole pile moves.
segments.tr: > Bestandsmanagement ist kein einzelnes Problem, sondern besteht aus vier Fragen: Welche Artikel sind am wichtigsten, wie wenig kann man lagern, wer übernimmt die Nachbestellung und wie schnell bewegt sich der gesamte Bestand?

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Heutiges Konzept

segments.src: Every business that stocks anything faces the same tension.
segments.tr: Jedes Unternehmen, das irgendetwas lagert, steht vor demselben Spannungsfeld.

segments.src: Hold too much, and cash sits on a shelf getting dusty (and paying rent).
segments.tr: Lagert man zu viel, liegt Kapital ungenutzt im Regal, verstaubt und kostet Miete.

segments.src: Hold too little, and you turn customers away.
segments.tr: Lagert man zu wenig, schickt man Kunden weg.

segments.src: The instinct is to solve this once, for everything.
segments.tr: Der Instinkt sagt, man solle das Problem ein für alle Mal für alles lösen.

segments.src: That's the mistake.
segments.tr: Genau das ist der Fehler.

segments.src: A hardware store carries $80 cordless drills and 3-cent washers in the same building.
segments.tr: Ein Baumarkt führt 80-Dollar-Akkubohrer und 3-Cent-Unterlegscheiben im selben Gebäude.

segments.src: Counting them with the same care is a waste of somebody's afternoon.
segments.tr: Beide mit der gleichen Sorgfalt zu zählen, verschwendet jemandes Nachmittag.

segments.src: Four tools handle this, and they stack:
segments.tr: Vier Werkzeuge helfen dabei, und sie bauen aufeinander auf:

segments.src: ABC analysis — decide where to spend attention.**
segments.tr: ABC-Analyse – entscheiden, wo die Aufmerksamkeit hingehört.**

segments.src: Rank every item by *annual dollar volume* (unit cost × units used per year), then split the list into three buckets.
segments.tr: Jeder Artikel wird nach dem *jährlichen Warenwert* (Stückkosten × jährlich verbrauchte Menge) eingestuft, anschließend wird die Liste in drei Klassen aufgeteilt.

segments.src: In a typical operation the pattern looks roughly like this:
segments.tr: In einem typischen Betrieb sieht das Muster ungefähr so aus:

segments.src: - **A items:** ~20% of the items, ~80% of the dollars. Watch closely, count often, forecast carefully.
segments.tr: - **A-Artikel:** etwa 20 % der Artikel, etwa 80 % der Werte. Eng überwachen, häufig zählen, sorgfältig prognostizieren.

segments.src: - **B items:** ~30% of the items, ~15% of the dollars. Moderate control.
segments.tr: - **B-Artikel:** etwa 30 % der Artikel, etwa 15 % der Werte. Mäßige Kontrolle.

segments.src: - **C items:** ~50% of the items, ~5% of the dollars. Order big, order rarely, don't agonize.
segments.tr: - **C-Artikel:** etwa 50 % der Artikel, etwa 5 % der Werte. Groß und selten bestellen, nicht lange grübeln.

segments.src: Those percentages are a rule of thumb (the Pareto principle), not a law — your actual curve might be 15/85 or 30/70.
segments.tr: Diese Prozentwerte sind eine Faustregel (das Pareto-Prinzip), kein Gesetz. Die tatsächliche Verteilung kann auch 15/85 oder 30/70 lauten.

segments.src: The point stands either way: attention is scarce, so aim it at the A items.
segments.tr: Die Aussage bleibt in jedem Fall gleich: Aufmerksamkeit ist knapp, also richtet man sie auf die A-Artikel.

segments.src: One caveat that trips people up: dollar volume isn't the only thing that matters.
segments.tr: Ein Vorbehalt, über den Leute häufig stolpern: Der Warenwert ist nicht das Einzige, was zählt.

segments.src: A 3-cent gasket that shuts down a production line is a C item by cost and an A item by consequence.
segments.tr: Eine 3-Cent-Dichtung, die eine Produktionslinie stilllegt, ist nach Kosten ein C-Artikel und nach Folgen ein A-Artikel.

segments.src: Good practice is to override the ranking for anything that's critical, hard to source, or has a long lead time.
segments.tr: Bewährte Praxis ist, die Rangfolge für alles außer Kraft zu setzen, was kritisch ist, schwer zu beschaffen ist oder lange Vorlaufzeiten hat.

segments.src: JIT (Just-In-Time) — shrink what you hold.**
segments.tr: JIT (Just-in-Time) – den Bestand verkleinern.**

segments.src: Developed inside Toyota's production system, JIT means material arrives right when it's needed, in the quantity needed.
segments.tr: JIT wurde im Produktionssystem von Toyota entwickelt und bedeutet: Material kommt genau dann, wenn es gebraucht wird, und in genau der benötigten Menge.

segments.src: Instead of forecasting demand and pushing inventory forward, downstream consumption *pulls* the next delivery.
segments.tr: Statt die Nachfrage vorherzusagen und Bestand auf Vorrat zu schieben, *zieht* der nachgelagerte Verbrauch die nächste Lieferung nach sich.

segments.src: The payoff is real: less cash tied up, less warehouse space, and defects surface fast because there's no buffer of bad parts to hide behind.
segments.tr: Der Nutzen ist real: weniger gebundenes Kapital, weniger Lagerfläche, und Fehler fallen schnell auf, weil kein Puffer fehlerhafter Teile sie verdeckt.

segments.src: The cost is equally real: JIT trades inventory buffer for supply-chain reliability.
segments.tr: Die Kosten sind genauso real: JIT tauscht Lagerpuffer gegen die Verlässlichkeit der Lieferkette.

segments.src: When something breaks upstream — a port backup, a chip shortage, a snowstorm on I-80 — you feel it in days, not months.
segments.tr: Wenn vorgelagert etwas bricht – ein Hafenstau, ein Chipmangel, ein Schneesturm auf der I-80 –, spürt man das in Tagen, nicht in Monaten.

segments.src: That's why many firms after 2020 shifted toward "just-in-case" hybrids: JIT for stable, high-volume items; deliberate buffers for anything single-sourced or coming from far away.
segments.tr: Deshalb sind nach 2020 viele Unternehmen zu „Just-in-Case“-Mischformen übergegangen: JIT für stabile Artikel mit hohem Volumen, bewusste Puffer für alles, was nur von einem Lieferanten kommt oder von weit her geliefert wird.

segments.src: VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory) — hand the reordering to the supplier.**
segments.tr: VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory) – die Nachbestellung an den Lieferanten übergeben.**

segments.src: Normally the buyer decides when to reorder.
segments.tr: Normalerweise entscheidet der Einkäufer, wann nachbestellt wird.

segments.src: Under VMI, the buyer shares actual sales and stock data, and the *supplier* decides what to ship and when, within agreed min/max levels.
segments.tr: Bei VMI teilt der Einkäufer tatsächliche Verkaufs- und Bestandsdaten, und der *Lieferant* entscheidet, was und wann geliefert wird, innerhalb vereinbarter Mindest- und Höchstbestände.

segments.src: Walmart and P&G built the best-known version of this in the late 1980s.
segments.tr: Walmart und P&G haben Ende der 1980er-Jahre die bekannteste Variante davon aufgebaut.

segments.src: Why it helps: the supplier finally sees real demand instead of guessing from lumpy purchase orders.
segments.tr: Warum das hilft: Der Lieferant sieht endlich die echte Nachfrage, statt aus unregelmäßigen Bestellungen zu raten.

segments.src: That damps the *bullwhip effect* — the way small wiggles in retail demand get amplified into wild swings in factory orders as they travel upstream.
segments.tr: Das dämpft den *Bullwhip-Effekt*: Kleine Schwankungen in der Einzelhandelsnachfrage werden entlang der Kette stromaufwärts zu wilden Ausschlägen bei den Fabrikbestellungen verstärkt.

segments.src: Ownership of the goods may or may not transfer at delivery; that's a contract detail worth pinning down, because it decides who eats the cost of unsold stock.
segments.tr: Ob das Eigentum an der Ware bei Lieferung übergeht, kann variieren; das ist ein Vertragsdetail, das man klären sollte, denn es entscheidet darüber, wer die Kosten für unverkaufte Ware trägt.

segments.src: Inventory turnover — measure whether any of it is working.**
segments.tr: Lagerumschlag – messen, ob der Bestand arbeitet.**

segments.src: Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold ÷ Average Inventory
segments.tr: Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold ÷ Average Inventory

segments.src: Days of Inventory   = 365 ÷ Inventory Turnover
segments.tr: Days of Inventory   = 365 ÷ Inventory Turnover

segments.src: Turnover says how many times per year you sell through and replace your entire stock.
segments.tr: Der Umschlag gibt an, wie oft pro Jahr der gesamte Bestand verkauft und wieder ersetzt wird.

segments.src: Use COGS, not revenue — revenue includes your margin, inventory is carried at cost, and mixing them inflates the number.
segments.tr: Man verwendet die COGS (Herstellungskosten der verkauften Waren), nicht den Umsatz. Der Umsatz enthält die Marge, Bestand wird aber zu Kosten bilanziert; eine Vermischung der beiden bläht die Zahl auf.

segments.src: Higher is generally better, but not infinitely.
segments.tr: Höher ist im Allgemeinen besser, aber nicht unbegrenzt.

segments.src: Turnover that's climbing while stockouts are also climbing means you've gone too lean.
segments.tr: Steigt der Umschlag, während auch Fehlbestände zunehmen, ist man zu schlank geworden.

segments.src: And the "good" number is entirely industry-specific: a grocery chain may turn 12–15 times a year, a jeweler 1–2.
segments.tr: Und die „gute“ Zahl ist völlig branchenabhängig: Eine Supermarktkette kommt vielleicht auf 12–15 Umschläge pro Jahr, ein Juwelier auf 1–2.

segments.src: Compare yourself to your own trend and your own sector, never to a headline benchmark from a different business.
segments.tr: Man vergleicht sich mit dem eigenen Trend und der eigenen Branche, nie mit einem Schlagzeilen-Benchmark aus einem anderen Geschäft.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Picture a three-location coffee shop in Austin.
segments.tr: Stellen Sie sich eine Kaffeebar mit drei Standorten in Austin vor.

segments.src: Annual COGS is $180,000, and average inventory on hand is $15,000.
segments.tr: Die jährlichen COGS betragen 180.000 $, der durchschnittlich vorhandene Bestand liegt bei 15.000 $.

segments.src: Turnover = 180,000 ÷ 15,000 = 12 times per year
segments.tr: Turnover = 180,000 ÷ 15,000 = 12 times per year

segments.src: Thirty days of stock — for a business selling milk and pastries.
segments.tr: Das sind dreißig Tage Vorrat – für ein Geschäft, das Milch und Gebäck verkauft.

segments.src: Something's off, and ABC analysis shows where.
segments.tr: Da stimmt etwas nicht, und die ABC-Analyse zeigt, wo.

segments.src: Espresso beans and oat milk are the **A items**: high cost, high volume, and they go stale.
segments.tr: Espressobohnen und Hafermilch sind die **A-Artikel**: hohe Kosten, hohes Volumen, und sie werden schnell alt.

segments.src: Flavored syrups are **B**.
segments.tr: Aromasirup ist **B**.

segments.src: Cups, lids, sleeves, and napkins are **C** — thousands of units, a few hundred dollars.

segments.src: So the owner splits the strategy.
segments.tr: Also teilt die Besitzerin die Strategie auf.

segments.src: Beans move to near-JIT: twice-weekly roaster deliveries sized to last week's actual pours, plus a small safety buffer for the Saturday rush.
segments.tr: Bohnen werden nahezu JIT beschafft: zweimal wöchentlich Lieferungen der Rösterei, abgestimmt auf den tatsächlichen Verbrauch der letzten Woche, plus ein kleiner Sicherheitspuffer für den Samstagsansturm.

segments.src: Pastries were already JIT — the bakery drops them at 5 a.m.
segments.tr: Gebäck war bereits JIT – die Bäckerei liefert es um 5 Uhr morgens

segments.src: daily.
segments.tr: täglich.

segments.src: Cups go the other way: one big quarterly order, because the storage closet is cheaper than the hassle of reordering.
segments.tr: Becher laufen in die andere Richtung: eine große Quartalsbestellung, denn der Lagerschrank ist billiger als der Aufwand ständiger Nachbestellungen.

segments.src: And that rack of chips and bottled drinks by the register?
segments.tr: Und das Regal mit Chips und Flaschengetränken neben der Kasse?

segments.src: The distributor's driver already walks in, eyeballs the shelf, and restocks it without anyone at the shop writing a purchase order.
segments.tr: Der Fahrer des Großhändlers kommt ohnehin vorbei, sieht ins Regal und füllt es auf, ohne dass im Laden jemand eine Bestellung schreibt.

segments.src: That's **VMI** — the same arrangement behind the vendor rep stocking the snack aisle at your local supermarket.
segments.tr: Das ist **VMI** – dieselbe Vereinbarung, mit der der Außendienstler des Herstellers das Snackregal in Ihrem Supermarkt bestückt.

segments.src: The shop stopped counting those items entirely.
segments.tr: Der Laden zählt diese Artikel überhaupt nicht mehr.

segments.src: Six months later: average inventory is $10,000, turnover is 18, days of inventory is about 20.
segments.tr: Sechs Monate später: Der durchschnittliche Bestand liegt bei 10.000 $, der Umschlag bei 18, die Reichweite bei etwa 20 Tagen.

segments.src: Roughly $5,000 in cash walked off the shelf and back into the register — and the espresso never ran out.
segments.tr: Rund 5.000 $ sind aus dem Regal wieder in die Kasse geflossen – und der Espresso ist nie ausgegangen.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Drei-Zeilen-Zusammenfassung

segments.src: 1. **ABC analysis** ranks items by annual dollar volume so your attention goes to the 20% of items carrying 80% of the money — with manual overrides for anything mission-critical.
segments.tr: 1. **ABC-Analyse** ordnet Artikel nach jährlichem Warenwert, damit die Aufmerksamkeit auf die 20 % der Artikel fällt, die 80 % des Geldes binden – mit manueller Übersteuerung für alles, was geschäftskritisch ist.

segments.src: 2. **JIT** replaces stock with reliable, frequent replenishment; **VMI** hands the reorder decision to a supplier who can finally see real demand.
segments.tr: 2. **JIT** ersetzt Bestand durch verlässliche, häufige Nachlieferung; **VMI** übergibt die Nachbestellentscheidung an einen Lieferanten, der die echte Nachfrage endlich sieht.

segments.src: 3. **Inventory turnover (COGS ÷ average inventory)** is the scoreboard — read it alongside stockout rate, because "faster" is only better until customers start leaving empty-handed.
segments.tr: 3. **Lagerumschlag (COGS ÷ durchschnittlicher Bestand)** ist die Anzeigetafel – man liest ihn zusammen mit der Fehlbestandsquote, denn „schneller“ ist nur besser, bis Kunden mit leeren Händen gehen.
